newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Sen. Kerry slightly ahead - poll.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Sen. Kerry slightly ahead - poll.

text.p: Mass. Sen. John Kerry has grabbed a marginal lead over challenger Gov. William Weld in the Senate race, according to a poll released Friday.

The Democratic incumbent leads 47 percent to 42 percent against his Republican rival, according to the Boston Herald/WCVB-TV daily tracking poll. The sample of 454 likely voters has a margin of error of plus or minus 4.6 percent.
The poll showed Weld, endorsed Wednesday by Reform Party presidential candidate Ross Perot, leading among independent voters by 50 percent to 35 percent for Kerry, the Boston Herald reported.
"There is continued movement by independent voters in Weld's favor," said pollster Kelly Myers of the University of New Hampshire Survey Center, which conducted the poll.
Kelly cautioned that the poll, which features an average of polling over the last three nights, is better at forecasting trends rather than precise outcomes.
Vice President Al Gore and other Democratic leaders turned out in force Friday to support Kerry, whose reelection is critical to Democratic hopes of recapturing the Senate.
Asked if he felt comfortable with his slight lead in the polls, Kerry said, "I just think it's full speed ahead, all-out. I'm heading towards the beach."
